units.learningObjective: Explain a mark using mixture concentration, brush load and paper condition separately.

exercise.action: Make the two load-test strokes above. Beside them, name which control changed and which two you kept similar.
constants: Dry paper of the same type
success: You can name the changed control without calling it dilution.
You can describe a visible difference or a useful inconclusive result.
exercise.transfer: Before a sky, petal or architectural wash, name the palette, brush and surface conditions separately.

units.waiting: Compare the marks again when both are dry; this may be on a later visit.
units.noVideoReason: Written/physical comparison is complete; no exact matching demonstration is sufficiently evidenced. Reflection needs no video.

units.learningObjective: Arrange a small, stable working area and enough mixture for an uninterrupted passage.

exercise.action: Rehearse moving from puddle to scrap, across one rectangle and back to the palette. Adjust the working area until the sequence is comfortable.
success: The sheet stays stable.
You can reach mixture, clean water and wiping material without crossing the painted passage.
exercise.transfer: Prepare the largest connected wash of your next subject before beginning it.

units.waiting: This preparation needs no drying wait.
units.noVideoReason: Written/physical comparison is complete; no exact matching demonstration is sufficiently evidenced. Reflection needs no video.

units.learningObjective: Repeat a loading action that produces a usable stroke without an uncontrolled final drop.

exercise.action: Make a row of three similar strokes, reloading before each. Keep the puddle unchanged and repeat the same unloading action.
exercise.variable: Loading action during initial adjustment; then repeat it
success: At least two strokes have comparable delivery.
You can identify whether any problem appears at the start, middle or end.
exercise.transfer: Use a scrap stroke before laying a clean light passage in your painting.

units.waiting: Let the comparison strokes dry before judging their final value.

previews.believedTopic: Broad brush/wash viewing proposal, not an isolated loading clip.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Locate actual wetting, belly loading, unloading and result context within the owner’s longer proposal; those actions are not individually witnessed in this record.

units.learningObjective: Change mark width deliberately while separating contact pressure from liquid load.

exercise.action: Compare the two rows. Change only the amount of hair in contact with the paper; keep the colour and loading sequence unchanged.
success: A narrow and a broader mark are distinguishable.
You can make both without flattening the hairs against the ferrule.
exercise.transfer: Use tip contact for a selected stem or edge and broader contact for the supporting mass.

units.waiting: Inspect dry texture after both rows have dried.
units.noVideoReason: Written/physical comparison is complete; no exact matching demonstration is sufficiently evidenced. Reflection needs no video.

units.learningObjective: Connect successive passes and finish without dragging a puddle through a drying area.

exercise.action: Paint one small rectangle using connected passes from the same mixture. On fresh scrap, repeat after adjusting only the load if the first wash pooled.
exercise.variable: Brush load, only between fresh attempts
success: Most adjacent passes connect without a dry gap.
The final edge is left without an uncontrolled pool, or you can identify why you stopped.
exercise.transfer: Use the wet-edge decision for a quiet sky or a single broad colour shape, without requiring every surface to be perfectly smooth.

units.waiting: Leave the patch alone until fully dry. Climate, sizing, sheet thickness and water load change the wait.

previews.believedTopic: The same longer wash proposal, not a newly verified short wash segment.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Confirm the actual pass sequence, wet bead and final result; no brush-action sub-boundaries have been supplied.

units.learningObjective: Produce distinguishable dry values while keeping brush delivery reasonably comparable.

exercise.action: Complete both three-swatch rows. Label the three concentrations in order after they dry, and circle any pair that is too similar to judge confidently.
constants: Swatch size and dry starting surface
success: Three dry value groups are recognisable, or a specific repeat test is planned.
Wet and dry swatches are not compared as if their conditions were equal.
exercise.transfer: Select a tested light or middle mixture for a petal, building plane or landscape passage.

units.waiting: Pause after painting the rows and compare on return; no fixed drying time is prescribed.
units.noVideoReason: Written/physical comparison is complete; no exact matching demonstration is sufficiently evidenced. Reflection needs no video.

units.learningObjective: Describe moisture from visible conditions rather than elapsed seconds.

exercise.action: Record two visible surface states on the scrap and predict which would let a similar stroke spread more. Test that prediction only on fresh comparison patches.
success: You distinguish standing water from an evenly damp surface.
You do not treat lost sheen as permission to scrub a partly drying wash.
exercise.transfer: Read a sky or foliage passage before deciding whether to connect another shape or leave it alone.

units.waiting: Observe over whatever interval your sheet needs; waiting is separate from active work.

previews.believedTopic: Owner-screened blending topic, beginning at 1:30; the endpoint is unknown.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Establish the complete moisture sequence and its endpoint without inferring dry or damp conditions from the title.

units.learningObjective: Connect an observed surface condition to a changed edge and spread.

exercise.action: Complete the dry/damp pair. Describe one observed condition and its boundary, without calling every soft transition a lost edge.
success: Both conditions are recorded, including an inconclusive difference.
You distinguish a soft transition from a genuinely disappearing contour.
exercise.transfer: Try the same comparison on a simple hill, leaf or abstract shape before using it in a painting.

units.waiting: Compare both dry; leave time between active comparisons for drying.

previews.believedTopic: Publisher’s wet-on-wet chapter hint; suggested comparison context only.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect actual surface moisture, load, spread and result; published chapter boundaries are not certified instructional clips.

previews.believedTopic: Publisher’s wet-on-dry chapter hint; compare with the separate wet-on-wet proposal.
previews.requiresDirectVerification: Inspect the actual dry-paper demonstration, setup and result. This is not evidence of a lost edge.

units.learningObjective: Use a visible symptom to select a plausible cause and a fresh controlled experiment.

exercise.action: Write a symptom, a plausible cause, the condition you checked and the single variable for a fresh repeat. Make the repeat only if the surface and materials are ready.
exercise.variable: One selected cause at a time
constants: All controls other than the selected one
success: The proposed cause is conditional, not certain from appearance alone.
You can explain when to stop instead of disturbing the current passage.
exercise.transfer: Use a margin or separate scrap to test a correction before applying it to an important painting.

units.waiting: Let the repeat dry before deciding whether it supports your hypothesis.
units.noVideoReason: Written/physical comparison is complete; no exact matching demonstration is sufficiently evidenced. Reflection needs no video.

units.learningObjective: Name one observed relationship, one remaining uncertainty and a small real-painting application.

exercise.action: Use the existing reflection field to record a relationship, a condition to repeat, an uncertainty and a small application to your own subject.
exercise.variable: Chosen handling in a new shape
constants: The tested mixture or loading sequence where useful
success: The reflection refers to visible evidence, not a guessed hidden process.
The proposed transfer names a physical action and an observation.
exercise.transfer: Use the chosen decision in the next guided landscape or your own subject; keep the other controls simple.

units.waiting: Begin this comparison when the relevant swatches are dry.
units.noVideoReason: Written/physical comparison is complete; no exact matching demonstration is sufficiently evidenced. Reflection needs no video.
